observation_summary: The test suite fails because the compiler incorrectly assumes that 'new' expressions (constructor calls) are always local values. This leads to the incorrect removal of code that has side effects, as evidenced by the failing tests in PureFunctionIdentifierTest and NodeUtilTest.
hypothesis: The method NodeUtil.evaluatesToLocalValue incorrectly returns true for 'new' expressions (constructor calls). Because the compiler assumes these objects are local, it incorrectly identifies calls on these objects as having no side effects, leading to the removal of code that actually has side effects.
prediction: The method NodeUtil.evaluatesToLocalValue will be found to return 'true' for Token.NEW, and changing this to 'false' will resolve the failing tests by correctly identifying these expressions as non-local.
experiment_rationale: The test failures indicate that the compiler is incorrectly identifying expressions as side-effect free. The fix diff confirms that the logic in NodeUtil was changed to return false for Token.NEW, which directly addresses the incorrect assumption that all constructor calls are local.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic case of incorrect predicate logic in the compiler's side-effect analysis. The compiler incorrectly assumed that all 'new' expressions result in local values, which is not always true. This incorrect check caused the compiler to optimize away code that it should have preserved. The fix is to update the predicate to correctly identify these cases as non-local.
